It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. #!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

LOG_DIR="/app/logs"
RULES_FILE="/app/rules/detection_rules.json"
REPORT_DIR="/app/reports"

# Parse JSON rules
function parse_rules() {
    # Use jq to extract rules array
    jq -r '.rules[] | .id + "|" + .pattern + "|" + .severity + "|" + (.threshold|tostring) + "|" + (.timeframe|tostring)' "$RULES_FILE
}

# Parse log line for auth.log
function parse_auth_line() {
    line="$1"
    # Extract timestamp (format: Apr 10 08:12:33)
    # Use regex to capture date and time
    if [[ "$line" =~ (\w{3}) (\d{2}) (\d{2}):(\d{2}):(\d{2}) ]]; then
        date="${BASH_REMATCH[1]} ${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
        time="${BASH_REMATCH[3]}:${BASH_REMATCH[4]}:${BASH_REMATCH[5]}"
        # Combine and convert to epoch seconds
        # We'll use date command to parse and convert
        # But for simplicity, we'll just keep string for now and compare with current time later.
        timestamp="$date $time"
        # Extract IP: "from <IP>"
        if [[ "$line" =~ from (\S+) ]]; then
            ip="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        else
            ip=""
        fi
    else
        timestamp=""
        ip=""
    fi
    echo "$timestamp|$ip|$line"
}

# Parse log line for http.log
function parse_http_line() {
    line="$1"
    # Extract timestamp: [10/Apr/2023:08:30:42 +0000]
    if [[ "$line" =~ \[(\d{2}/\w{3}/\d{4}):(\d{2}):(\d{2}):(\d{2}) ]]; then
        date="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        time="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}:${BASH_REMATCH[3]}:${BASH_REMATCH[4]}"
        timestamp="$date $time"
        # Extract IP: first token after timestamp
        ip=$(echo "$line" | awk '{print $1}')
    else
        timestamp=""
        ip=""
    fi
    echo "$timestamp|$ip|$line"
}

# Main detection
function main() {
    # Ensure report directory exists
    mkdir -p "$REPORT_DIR"
    
    # Get current time in epoch seconds
    current_time=$(date +%s)
    
    # Parse rules
    rules=$(parse_rules)
    while IFS="|" read -r rule_id pattern severity threshold timeframe; do
        # Initialize data for this rule
        # We'll collect matches per IP: ip -> count
        declare -A ip_counts
        # Scan auth.log
        while IFS= read -r auth_line; do
            parsed=$(parse_auth_line "$auth_line")
            if [[ -n "$parsed" ]]; then
                ts_ip_line=$(echo "$parsed" | tr '|' '\n')
                timestamp=$(echo "$ts_ip_line" | head -1)
                ip=$(echo "$ts_ip_line" | tail -1)
                if [[ "$timestamp" =~ ^[A-Za-z]{3} [0-9]{2} [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$ ]]; then
                    # Convert timestamp to epoch seconds
                    epoch=$(date -d "$timestamp" +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
                    if [[ $epoch -ge $((current_time - timeframe)) ]]; then
                        if [[ "$line" =~ $pattern ]]; then
                            ((ip_counts[$ip]++))
                        fi
                    fi
                fi
            fi
        done < <(grep -h "$pattern" "$LOG_DIR/auth.log")
        
        # Scan http.log
        while IFS= read -r http_line; do
            parsed=$(parse_http_line "$http_line")
            if [[ -n "$parsed" ]]; then
                ts_ip_line=$(echo "$parsed" | tr '|' '\n')
                timestamp=$(echo "$ts_ip_line" | head -1)
                ip=$(echo "$ts_ip_line" | tail -1)
                if [[ "$timestamp" =~ ^[A-Za-z]{3} [0-9]{2} [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$ ]]; then
                    epoch=$(date -d "$timestamp" +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
                    if [[ $epoch -ge $((current_time - timeframe)) ]]; then
                        if [[ "$http_line" =~ $pattern ]]; then
                            ((ip_counts[$ip]++))
                        fi
                    fi
                fi
            fi
        done < <(grep -h "$pattern" "$LOG_DIR/http.log")
        
        # Prepare data for JSON
        # Build IPs list
        ips=$(echo "${!ip_counts[@]}" | tr '\n' ',' | sed 's/,$//')
        # Count total matches
        total=$(echo "${#ip_counts[@]}" | awk '{sum += $1} END {print sum}')
        
        # Add to events array
        # We'll store in temporary files for JSON generation
        echo "$rule_id|$severity|$total|$ips" >> "$REPORT_DIR/events.txt"
        
        # For alert generation, we need to check threshold
        if [[ $total -ge $threshold ]]; then
            echo "$rule_id|$severity|$total|$ips" >> "$REPORT_DIR/alerts.txt"
        fi
    done <<< "$rules"
    
    # Generate report.json
    if [[ -f "$REPORT_DIR/events.txt" ]]; then
        # Build statistics dictionary
        stats=$(while IFS="|" read -r rule_id severity total ips; do
            echo "$rule_id:$total"
        done < "$REPORT_DIR/events.txt" | tr '\n' ',' | sed 's/,$//')
        
        # Build events array
        events=$(cat "$REPORT_DIR/events.txt" | while IFS="|" read -r rule_id severity total ips; do
            echo "    {\n      "id": \"$rule_id\",\n      "severity": \"$severity\",\n      "matches": $total,\n      "ips": \"$ips\"\n    },"
        done | sed '$s/,$//')
        
        # Create report.json
        cat > "$REPORT_DIR/report.json" << EOF
{
  "timestamp": "$(date -u +'%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')",
  "events": [
$events
  ],
  "statistics": {
    $stats
  }
}
EOF
    fi
    
    # Generate alert.json
    if [[ -f "$REPORT_DIR/alerts.txt" ]]; then
        alerts=$(cat "$REPORT_DIR/alerts.txt" | while IFS="|" read -r rule_id severity total ips; do
            echo "    {\n      "id": \"$rule_id\",\n      "severity": \"$severity\",\n      "matches": $total,\n      "ips": \"$ips\"\n    },"
        done | sed '$s/,$//')
        
        cat > "$REPORT_DIR/alert.json" << EOF
{
  "timestamp": "$(date -u +'%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')",
  "alerts": [
$alerts
  ]
}
EOF
    fi
    
    echo "Detection complete. Reports written to $REPORT_DIR/"
}

# Execute main
main
EOF

- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- Most bash commands should end with a newline (\n) to cause them to execute

  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command

- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings

function parse_rules() {

}

        time="${BASH_REMATCH[3]}:${BASH_REMATCH[4]}:${BASH_REMATCH[5]}"
        # Combine and convert to epoch seconds

        # Extract IP: "from <IP>"

            ip="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        else
            ip=""
        fi
    else
        timestamp=""
        ip=""
    fi
    echo "$timestamp|$ip|$line"
}

}

        date="${BASH_REMATCH[1]} ${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
        time="${BASH_REMATCH[3]}:${BASH_REMATCH[4]}:${BASH_REMATCH[5]}"
        timestamp="$date $time"
        # Extract IP: "from <IP>"
        if [[ "$line" =~ from (\S+) ]]; then
            ip="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        else
            ip=""
        fi
    else
        timestamp=""
        ip=""
    fi
    echo "$timestamp|$ip|$line"
}

function parse_http_line() {
    line="$1"

    if [[ "$line" =~ \[(\d{2}/\w{3}/\d{4}):(\d{2}):(\d{2}):(\d{2}) ]]; then
        date="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"

        timestamp="$date $time"

        ip=""

set -euo pipefail

LOG_DIR="/app/logs"
RULES_FILE="/app/rules/detection_rules.json"
REPORT_DIR="/app/reports"

# Parse JSON rules
function parse_rules() {
    # Use jq to extract rules array
    jq -r '.rules[] | .id + "|" + .pattern + "|" + .severity + "|" + (.threshold|tostring) + "|" + (.timeframe|tostring)' "$RULES_FILE
}

    line="$1"

        time="${BASH_REMATCH[3]}:${BASH_REMATCH[4]}:${BASH_REMATCH[5]}"
        # Combine and convert to epoch seconds
        # We'll use date command to parse and convert
        # But for simplicity, we'll just keep string for now and compare with current time later.
        timestamp="$date $time"
        # Extract IP: "from <IP>"

            ip="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        else
            ip=""
        fi
    else
        timestamp=""
        ip=""
    fi
    echo "$timestamp|$ip|$line"
}

# Parse log line for http.log

    line="$1"
    # Extract timestamp: [10/Apr/2023:08:30:42 +0000]

    else

        ip=""
    fi
    echo "$timestamp|$ip|$line"
}

# Main detection

    # Ensure report directory exists
    mkdir -p "$REPORT_DIR"
    
    # Get current time in epoch seconds

    # Parse rules

        # Initialize data for this rule

            parsed=$(parse_auth_line "$auth_line")

                    if [[ $epoch -ge $((current_time - timeframe)) ]]; then
                        if [[ "$line" =~ $pattern ]]; then

            if [[ -n "$parsed" ]]; then
                ts_ip_line=$(echo "$parsed" | tr '|' '\n')
                timestamp=$(echo "$ts_ip_line" | head -1)
                ip=$(echo "$ts_ip_line" | tail -1)
                if [[ "$timestamp" =~ ^[A-Za-z]{3} [0-9]{2} [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$ ]]; then

                        if [[ "$http_line" =~ $pattern ]]; then

        # Count total matches

        # Add to events array
        # We'll store in temporary files for JSON generation
        echo "$rule_id|$severity|$total|$ips" >> "$REPORT_DIR/events.txt"
        
        # For alert generation, we need to check threshold
        if [[ $total -ge $threshold ]]; then
            echo "$rule_id|$severity|$total|$ips" >> "$REPORT_DIR/alerts.txt"

  "events": [

  ],

    $stats
  }
}
EOF

  ]
}

    fi

main
